requirements.requirement: Make the currently supplied DNS nameservers persistent on node1.
requirements.summary: The sole supplied resolver, 10.100.91.1, was observed before configuration, saved in the active NetworkManager profile, remained effective after reapplication, and persisted in both the profile and regenerated resolver configuration after a verified reboot. DNS resolution worked before and after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: Add infra.test as the system search domain on node1.
requirements.summary: The active NetworkManager profile and effective /etc/resolv.conf contained infra.test after application and again after the verified reboot, directly demonstrating persistence.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The restart protocol is complete and coherent: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the scheduled restart, changed boot identity from d6298ced-a924-4ce7-bbed-0fb8179eda8e to f4ad7087-1a96-444d-9465-0baac3fd7396, and recovered NetworkManager, connectivity, persistent DNS settings, and successful DNS resolution. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The only configuration mutation, modifying and reapplying the active NetworkManager profile, directly established the requested DNS state. Scheduling one reboot directly tested persistence and fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol. All other commands were read-only verification or bounded restart polling. The post-executor snapshot shows no failed services, package damage, unexpected listeners, or non-routine temporary-file residue; observed PID and systemd-private-directory changes are normal consequences of the reboot.
